title: zForth on CP/M-80 (Z80) — the DOS-native Forth, on a non-DOS target

components.source: src/zforth/zforth.c + forth/core.zf (zevv/zForth) + cpmmain.c + crt0.s, built with SDCC (z80)

toolchain.target: cpm80 (Z80 CP/M 2.2 .COM, 32-bit integer cell, BDOS console out)

notes: The SAME tiny Forth the lab ships as a DOS program (projects/forth-dos), recompiled for a NON-DOS target. zForth's DOS build uses float cells and printf/sscanf/fopen, none SDCC-z80 friendly; this build uses a 32-bit INTEGER cell (division is integer: 7/2 == 3 — the one deliberate semantic gap versus the float-cell DOS build), sends output through BDOS function 2 (cpmmain.c, no printf), embeds the Forth program as a C string (no CP/M file I/O), and compiles with ZF_ENABLE_TRACE 0 (no va_list). The committed prog.fth is the exact canonical shape the Code-tab blocks->Forth transpiler emits (a `: banner ;` word, `7 7 *`, and a counted `( repeat )` begin/until loop), so this proves that transpiler output — the language — runs on the Z80 CP/M machine, not only on the 8086 DOS bench. build.sh rebuilds FORTH.COM byte-for-byte. crt0.s is BrickWright's (BSD-2-Clause, from projects/cpm-software). proof.mjs boots it on the bw-board z80 machine via runMediaBundle with the same minimal BDOS console shim cpm-software uses.
